newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar ends mixed, nearbys at day's pea.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar ends mixed, nearbys at day's pea.

text.p: London's white sugar futures market ended mixed with nearby positions holding at or near their day's peaks on steady New York raws.
But movements on both spreads and premiums remained tight before New York's March raws expiry.
Spot May finished just 10 cents up at $306.20 a tonne after a high of $306.50.
Earlier trade and broker selling drove the spot contract down to a low of $304.00.
Volume totalled 1,678 lots. The options pit saw brisk activity with some 2,100 lots, dominated by May $300 calls, changing hands.
May/August hovered between premium and discount as May weakened in a continued technical reaction to last week's strength.
Traders said they expected the spread to narrow to a discount as buying had been noted at 50 cents under par.
Limited activity was reported on the white premium and was mainly a function of more volatile trading in New York before the March expiry at the end of the week.
"New York has been moving and London hasn't -- and next morning London gets sold down to pull it back into line," another trader said.

Technically, the outlook for May whites is gradually turning In physical news, Iraq has postponed its tender to buy sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal until February 28 but the quantity required is still unclear.
Syria tenders on Wednesday to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws, both amounts for April shipment. Results are to be made known on Thursday.
